arguments.content:
# Hosted API capability launch readiness

Decision owner: Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
Capability: Standard Cost Model Spec + internal Cost Model API v1  
Revision: 1 — product and delivery baseline  
Decision status: Pending cross-functional evidence

## Capability and supported scope

The planned capability is an internal, versioned Cost Model API used by Console, Optimize, billing hooks, and finance reporting to share canonical inference-cost primitives. V1 includes per-request estimates, bounded aggregated breakdowns, guarded what-if projections, schema negotiation, telemetry input contracts, and feature-flagged integrations. It is not a public customer API, a billing system of record, a pricing calculator, or a promise that Console grand totals equal invoices. [PM-1482](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/PM-1482-standard-cost-model-prd.json>) [PRD](</knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json>)

## Satisfied product gates

- Product scope, non-goals, canonical taxonomy, success measures, and phased rollout are documented; PM-1482 is Done with required stakeholder approvals recorded. [PM-1482](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/PM-1482-standard-cost-model-prd.json>)
- The internal service skeleton, internal-only routing, scoped service principals, tenant resolution, audit fields, endpoint envelopes, initial bounds, and observability hooks are complete in ENG-4821. Owner: Benji Okafor; accountable: Ethan Park. [ENG-4821](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821-cost-model-service-skeleton.json>)
- Console adoption is feature-flagged and has a legacy fallback requirement; v1 explicitly bounds synchronous work and keeps ad hoc analytics out of the hot path. Owners: Chloe Martin, Jada Williams, Ethan Park. [Platform decision thread](</knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1768427740.json>)

## Unresolved delivery items

- Confirm schema/codegen completion and compatibility evidence for ENG-4822. Owner: Thomas Baird.
- Complete shared-client adoption and confirm timeout/retry/schema-negotiation behavior across Console and Optimize. Owner: Benji Okafor.
- Complete drift SLI, dashboards, alerts, and SRE approval in ENG-4827. Owner: Rafael Mendes.
- Complete billing-hook alignment, replay evidence, intentional-difference documentation, and Finance/Telemetry/Auth reviews in ENG-4832. Owners: Cole Summers, Laura Bennett, Nadia Rahman, Kaitlyn Nguyen.
- Close PRD checklist items whose authoritative Confluence page remains in review, including SLO/on-call, support enablement, and Finance mapping. Owners: Marissa Cole and named gate owners. [PRD](</knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json>)

## Preliminary recommendation

Pending operational, security, release, customer, and support evidence. No launch date is asserted.

## Revision history

- Revision 1: established capability, product gates, scope, delivery gaps, and owners from product and engineering evidence.

# Hosted API capability launch readiness

Decision owner: Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
Capability: Standard Cost Model Spec + internal Cost Model API v1  
Revision: 2 — operations, security, and release evidence  
Decision status: Conditional-go candidate for a tightly scoped flagged cohort; no broad launch

## Capability and supported launch scope

The capability is an internal, versioned Cost Model API that supplies canonical inference-cost primitives to Console, Optimize, billing hooks, and finance reporting. V1 supports request-bounded estimates, bounded reads from precomputed rollups, guarded what-if projections, schema negotiation, telemetry contracts, and feature-flagged integrations. It is not a public Hosted API, billing system of record, pricing calculator, ad hoc analytics engine, or guarantee that Console usage totals equal invoice grand totals. [PM-1482](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/PM-1482-standard-cost-model-prd.json>) [PRD](</knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json>) [Platform decision](</knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1769536063.json>)

Supported launch scope is limited to internal callers and an allowlisted Console cohort behind `console_cost_breakdown_use_cost_model_api`, with legacy aggregation fallback, bounded default views, cached last-known UI data, explicit freshness/partial-result states, and one-click flag rollback. Optimize or billing expansion must remain gated until their own acceptance evidence is complete.

## Gate assessment

| Gate | State | Evidence and owner |
|---|---|---|
| Product definition and stakeholder alignment | Satisfied | PM-1482 is Done and records required stakeholder approvals. Owner: Talia Benson / Marissa Cole. [PM-1482](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/PM-1482-standard-cost-model-prd.json>) |
| Internal service foundation | Satisfied | ENG-4821 is Done: internal-only exposure, service auth, tenant middleware, audit fields, endpoint scaffolding, bounds, and base observability. Owner: Benji Okafor; accountable: Ethan Park. [ENG-4821](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821-cost-model-service-skeleton.json>) |
| Scope and complexity controls | Satisfied for limited scope | Request-level synchronous calls and bounded rollup reads are accepted; unbounded filtering and raw synchronous aggregation are excluded. Owner: Ethan Park / Thomas Baird. [Platform decision](</knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1768427740.json>) [Performance budget](</knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/cost-model-performance-budget.json>) |
| Client build/CI | Satisfied at library level | Shared client PR reports passing build, unit, lint, API compatibility, license, and SAST checks. Adoption verification remains separate. Owner: Benji Okafor. [PR 28462](</knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-28462-add-cost-model-client-library.json>) |
| Reliability validation | Blocked for broad launch | ENG-4827 is In Progress; formal SLO/alerts/approval evidence is not complete. Owner: Rafael Mendes. [ENG-4827](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4827-cost-model-drift-sli-and-alerts.json>) |
| Security authorization | Blocked | ENG-4821 requires security review and implements internal OIDC/mTLS, allowlisted service principals, tenant enforcement, cross-tenant rejection, and audit fields, but no authoritative final security approval was found. Owner: Kaitlyn Nguyen / Security reviewer; accountable: Ethan Park. [ENG-4821](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821-cost-model-service-skeleton.json>) |
| Release readiness | Blocked for broad launch | Feature flags and fallback exist, but the evidence set does not establish an accepted canary report, two-person promotion approval, or completed 48-hour regression-free observation for this capability. Owner: Chloe Martin / Rafael Mendes / release approver. [Console adoption](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4825-console-cost-breakdown-adoption.json>) |
| Finance/billing alignment | Blocked for broad launch | ENG-4832 still required replay evidence, intentional-difference docs, and Telemetry/Auth/Finance reviews in its latest cited update. Owners: Cole Summers, Nadia Rahman, Kaitlyn Nguyen, Laura Bennett. [ENG-4832](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4832-billing-hooks-alignment-with-cost-model.json>) |

## Operational gates and rollback criteria

Before any cohort increase:

- Demonstrate endpoint SLO and error-budget compliance for the intended request shapes; publish latency, errors, cache hit rate, request-shape/cardinality, telemetry freshness, and drift panels. Owner: Rafael Mendes.
- Exercise Console degradation: cached last-known value plus banner for aggregate failure; hide request detail rather than failing the page; legacy fallback retained. Owners: Jada Williams / Chloe Martin.
- Enforce server bounds, per-tenant cache quotas, top-K plus “other,” deterministic ordering, client timeouts, bounded retries with jitter, and request coalescing. Owners: Ethan Park / Benji Okafor / Thomas Baird.
- Stop or roll back if latency exceeds the accepted SLO, 504s recur, request-shape saturation appears, cross-tenant/auth audit failures occur, drift breaches the approved lag-aware threshold, or customer-facing totals lack freshness/estimate labeling. Owner: Rafael Mendes; rollback operator: Console release owner.

## Blockers and remaining approvals

1. Security: recorded production authorization for the internal service controls and audit evidence.
2. SRE: approved SLO/SLIs, alert thresholds, on-call assignment, runbook, and successful rollback exercise.
3. Release: accepted limited-cohort canary evidence and two-person authorization for any expansion.
4. Delivery: verified completion/adoption evidence for schema compatibility, client behavior, caching/bounds, and Console UX fallback.
5. Finance/Telemetry/Auth: accepted ENG-4832 replay and mapping evidence.

## Evidence-backed next steps

- Rafael Mendes: finish ENG-4827; attach SLO approval, dashboards, alert routing, and rollback-drill result.
- Kaitlyn Nguyen plus Security: record final review of identity, tenant isolation, service-principal scopes, audit fields, and negative cross-tenant tests.
- Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Thomas Baird: attach load-test and request-bound evidence, including cache hit rate and deterministic top-K behavior.
- Chloe Martin and Jada Williams: demonstrate flagged fallback, labeling, freshness state, request coalescing, and safe default groupings.
- Cole Summers, Nadia Rahman, Laura Bennett: complete replay reconciliation and sign off intentional Console-versus-invoice differences.
- Release approvers: run and accept a limited-cohort canary before increasing exposure.

## Recommendation

**Conditional-go only for an internal/allowlisted, feature-flagged cohort with legacy fallback; no-go for broad Hosted/Console rollout.** The limited scope is supportable because product scope and the internal service foundation are established and rollback containment exists. Broad launch is not reviewable as go until security authorization, SRE readiness, canary acceptance, and Finance/Telemetry alignment are recorded. No launch date is proposed.

## Revision history

- Revision 1: established capability, product gates, scope, delivery gaps, and owners from product and engineering evidence.
- Revision 2: incorporated operations, security, and release evidence; narrowed supported scope; added operational gates, blockers, approvals, next steps, and a conditional-go candidate.

# Hosted API capability launch readiness

Decision owner: Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
Capability: Standard Cost Model Spec + internal Cost Model API v1  
Revision: 3 — final reviewable decision  
Decision: **Conditional-go for a tightly scoped, allowlisted cohort; no-go for broad rollout**

## Decision summary

Proceed only with internal callers and an explicitly allowlisted Console cohort behind `console_cost_breakdown_use_cost_model_api`, retaining legacy aggregation fallback and one-click disablement. Do not expand broadly until the blocking security, SRE, release, delivery, and Finance/Telemetry approvals below are recorded. No launch date is proposed.

The capability supplies canonical inference-cost primitives to Console, Optimize, billing hooks, and finance reporting. V1 supports request-bounded estimates, bounded reads from precomputed rollups, guarded what-if projections, schema negotiation, telemetry contracts, and feature-flagged integrations. It is not a public customer API, billing system of record, pricing calculator, ad hoc analytics engine, or guarantee that Console usage totals equal invoice grand totals. [PM-1482](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/PM-1482-standard-cost-model-prd.json>) [PRD](</knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json>) [Platform decision](</knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1769536063.json>)

## Supported launch scope

Allowed:

- Internal service-to-service callers using scoped identities.
- A named, allowlisted Console cohort with bounded standard views.
- Request-level estimate/breakdown and synchronous reads from precomputed rollups only.
- Explicit partial/freshness/estimate states, cached last-known UI data, legacy fallback, and flag rollback.
- Customer messaging that distinguishes standardized usage primitives from contract-level invoice items.

Excluded until separately approved:

- General availability or all-paid-account enablement.
- Direct public customer access to the Cost Model API.
- Unbounded filters, raw synchronous aggregation, or high-cardinality ad hoc analytics.
- Treating Cost Model output as invoice grand total.
- Optimize, billing, or larger Console expansion without their own acceptance evidence.

Owner: Benji Okafor. [PR 28462](</knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-28462-add-cost-model-client-library.json>) |
| Customer validation | Partial | Northbridge confirmed usability after the latency mitigation, and later usage reconciliation matched billing usage subtotal within 0.4% after backfill. This validates containment and explainability for one enterprise account, not broad readiness. Owners: Chloe Martin / Rafael Mendes. ## Blockers and remaining approvals

1. **Security authorization:** final production approval for service identity, principal scopes, tenant isolation, negative cross-tenant tests, and access audit evidence.
2. **SRE readiness:** approved SLO/SLIs, alert thresholds, pager ownership, published runbook, cache/request-shape panels, and a successful rollback exercise.
3. **Permanent performance controls:** server caching/memoization, cache-size and per-tenant guards, bounded defaults, deterministic top-K, request coalescing, and bounded retry behavior proven under intended cohort load.
4. **Release acceptance:** documented limited-cohort canary, stable observation against accepted thresholds, and two-person authorization for exposure increase.
5. **Finance/Telemetry/Auth acceptance:** accepted replay and mapping evidence for ENG-4832 and stable documentation of intentional invoice differences.
6. **Support/product completion:** rename ambiguous totals, add invoice-reconciliation and taxonomy links, display telemetry backfill/freshness states, and complete support enablement.

## Accepted launch criteria

A reviewer may approve expansion only when all of the following are evidenced:

- Scope remains internal and feature-flagged until broad approval.
- Authenticated, authorized, tenant-isolated access and audit records pass Security review.
- Intended request shapes meet approved latency, availability, error-budget, freshness, and lag-aware drift thresholds.
- Request bounds, caching, top-K, client timeouts, retry controls, coalescing, graceful degradation, and legacy rollback are tested.
- A limited cohort completes the approved observation window without critical regression or rollback trigger.
- Console copy and exports clearly say “usage” and explain excluded fees, commitments, credits, adjustments, and taxes.
- Console usage reconciles to the billing usage subtotal within the accepted, lag-corrected tolerance; contract-level invoice items remain separately explained.
- Support owns a published troubleshooting/reconciliation path; SRE owns the pager/runbook; Security, SRE, Release, Finance/Telemetry/Auth, Product, and Console approvals are recorded.

## Operational stop and rollback criteria

Pause exposure growth or disable the flag if any approved SLO is breached; 504s or retry amplification recur; saturation or high-cardinality shapes escape bounds; cache/request-shape telemetry is unavailable; freshness or estimate labeling is absent; drift exceeds the approved lag-aware threshold; cross-tenant/auth/audit tests fail; or support cannot explain a customer-visible total.

Rollback owner: Console release operator. Incident owner: Platform Control Plane on-call. Decision owner for re-entry: Ethan Park with the blocking gate owner.

## Evidence-backed next steps

- Rafael Mendes: finish ENG-4827; attach SLO approval, dashboards, alert routing, pager ownership, and rollback-drill result.
- Kaitlyn Nguyen plus Security: record production authorization and negative tenant-isolation/audit results.
- Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Thomas Baird: attach load-test evidence for permanent caching, bounds, deterministic top-K, and client safeguards.
- Chloe Martin and Jada Williams: demonstrate fallback, safe defaults, usage/invoice labeling, freshness/backfill state, and request coalescing.
- Cole Summers, Nadia Rahman, Laura Bennett: complete and approve replay reconciliation and intentional-difference documentation.
- Release approvers: execute and accept the limited-cohort canary before any exposure increase.
- Support lead: publish the reusable reconciliation guide and escalation ownership.

## Recommendation rationale

**Conditional-go for the contained cohort; no-go for broad rollout.** Product definition, service foundations, CI, feature flags, and a working fallback make a limited cohort defensible. The latency incident proves that request shape, caching, retries, and saturation are launch-critical rather than theoretical. The invoice case proves that customer trust depends on permanent product copy and support guidance. Because final Security authorization, SRE approval, permanent-control evidence, canary acceptance, and Finance/Telemetry/Auth signoff are not all present, broader enablement would be unsupported.

## Revision history

- **Revision 1 — product and delivery baseline:** established the capability, satisfied product gates, supported scope, unresolved delivery work, and owners.
- **Revision 2 — operations, security, and release:** added operational gates, narrowed supported scope, identified approval blockers, and formed the conditional-go candidate.
- **Revision 3 — final decision:** incorporated customer and support evidence from the latency and invoice-reconciliation cases; finalized blockers, accepted launch criteria, stop conditions, next steps, and the conditional-go/no-broad-rollout recommendation.

arguments.outcome: Conditional-go for contained cohort; no-go for broad rollout pending all accepted launch criteria.
arguments.summary: Decision: conditional-go only for internal callers and a tightly scoped allowlisted Console cohort behind a feature flag with legacy fallback; no-go for broad rollout. Expansion requires recorded Security authorization; approved SRE SLOs, alerts, pager/runbook and rollback drill; permanent caching/bounds/top-K/client safeguards proven under load; accepted limited-cohort canary and two-person promotion approval; Finance/Telemetry/Auth replay and mapping acceptance; clear usage-versus-invoice labeling and support reconciliation guidance. Stop or roll back on SLO breach, recurring 504/retry amplification, saturation or escaped cardinality, missing freshness/estimate labeling, excessive lag-aware drift, failed tenant/auth/audit controls, or unsupported customer totals.
